errors.text_span: The categories are grouped into three layers: Signal Layer (4.3%), Cultural Layer (14.1%), and Semantic Layer (41.2%), with the largest remaining portion labeled as Perception Layer (40.4%).
errors.evidence: The sentence states there are "three layers" but then proceeds to list all four main categories shown in the chart. The phrasing is confusing and structurally incorrect.

errors.text_span: The Signal Layer includes Anomaly Detection, Acoustic Quality Analysis, Audio Difference Analysis, and Signal Layer.
errors.evidence: The description incorrectly lists the parent category "Signal Layer" as one of its own sub-categories.

errors.text_span: The Cultural Layer comprises Imagination, Culture of Speaker, Asthetic Analysis, Professional Knowl & Reasoning, and Spatial Analysis.
errors.evidence: The description incorrectly assigns "Spatial Analysis" to the "Cultural Layer". In the chart, "Spatial Analysis" is clearly a sub-category of the "Perception Layer".

errors.text_span: with the Perception Layer occupying the largest area, followed by the Semantic Layer
errors.evidence: The description incorrectly states that the Perception Layer is the largest. The percentage labels clearly show the Semantic Layer is the largest (41.2%) compared to the Perception Layer (40.4%).

errors.text_span: The segments are visually arranged in a descending order of size
errors.evidence: The segments representing the main layers are not visually arranged in descending order of size. Following the chart clockwise from the top, the order is Signal (4.3%), Semantic (41.2%), Perception (40.4%), and Cultural (14.1%), which is not a sorted order.
The description claims the chart has a legend, but there is no separate legend box. All labels are directly on or next to the chart's slices.

errors.text_span: percentage labels provided for the three layers
errors.evidence: The description states that percentages are provided for three layers, but the chart shows percentages for all four main layers: Signal Layer (4.3%), Cultural Layer (14.1%), Semantic Layer (41.2%), and Perception Layer (40.4%).

The description fails to mention the distinct colors of the segments, which is a key visual feature and was requested in the prompt ('color (if distinguishable)'). Specifically, it omits that the 'Perception Layer' is dark blue, while the other layers are a lighter blue, and the outer ring uses shades of light blue and gray.
